newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The winds of change continued to sweep through the game of rugby union yesterday as controversial changes were announced to Australia's traditional green and gold jersey, which the national side has been wearing since 1961. Officials have cited a new profssional era of the game as the reason why the strip was changed. Page 20.

The Australian Rugby League remains confident that the success of its season will not be affected by which channel wins the rights to televise the free-to-air Super League games. The decision on the carrier, which could come as soon as tomorrow, still remins a mystery, but speculation continues that the ARL's biggest backer, Channel Nine, could be successful in bidding for at least a portion of the rights. Page 18.

Australia is confident it can go out on a winning note in its final one day match against Pakistan in Melbourne today. It is the last chance the Melbourne public will get to see their national side, but some pundits believe that given Australia's recent poor one day form and the attraction of the Australian Open over the road, today's crowd could be considerably down. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League chairman Ken Arthurson said yesterday that Channel Nine's chief executive David Leckie's position on the ARL Board could be in jeopardy if it is successful in its bid to televise Super League's free-to-air games. Arthurson confirmed that the ARL's administrative structure may be complicated by an agreement between the station and Super League. Page 43.

Despite New South Wales jockeys ruling out the prospect of further strikes in protest at pay levels, a delegation will meet today with New South Wales Racing Minister Richard Face after rejecting an estimated A$15 a-ride increase made yesterday. Page 43.

Australian cricket vice-captain Ian Healy stood behind his embattled captain Mark Taylor yesterday, saying that the skipper's form was only a minor reason for the team's form slump. Healy also deflected questions about him becoming captain, saying it would be difficult to both captain and wicket-keep at Test level. Page 43.
THE AGE

World number one Steffi Graf had a difficult time of it yesterday as she struggled to win her way into the third round of the Australian Open. Her day soured further when it was revealed that prosecutors have asked her father be jailed for nearly seven yers on tax evasion charges. Page B8.

In a sensational game of tennis at the Australian Open yesterday, young Aussie duo Wayne Arthurs and Jon Ireland won an epic game of doubles; 3-6, 6-3, 29-27. The game lasted nearly eight hours (including rain delay), and was watched by an ever-growing crwd of bewildered supporters. Page B8.

The player list in the Australian Masters continues to grow as former US Masters winner Larry Mize agreed to join fellow American Tiger Woods in what is becoming one of the largest golf tournaments in Australia in recent history. It is the first time Miz will play in Australia. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australia's main hope in the singles draw at the Australian Open, Todd Woodbridge, won his way into the third round yesterday after beating Frenchman Stephane Simian. He now faces a meeting with Wimbledon finalist MaliVai Washington. Page 84.

Fifth seeded women's player Anke Huber was forced to postpone her match in the Open yesterday, after her mother collapsed outside the players' lounge. Huber's opponent had no objection to shifting the clash to 10am today. Page 85.

Clay court specialist Richard Fromberg fell to seventh-seed Thomas Enquivst in the third round of the men's singles in the Australian Open yesterday. The game, which Fromberg had several chances of taking control of, was another to come out and question the weight of the tournament's balls. Page 84.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

In what appears to be a sign of things to come, it has been revealed that Australia's cricket tour of South Africa will not be broadcast on free-to-air television next month. Pay-TV giant Foxtel will broadcast the three Tests and seven one day matches. Page 82.

Kangaroo rugby league winger Willie Carne looks set to change codes and play rugby union this year. The talented winger has received an offer from the Queensland Rugby Union to switch codes in 1997. Page 83.

New AFL club Port Power has said that it is not interested in dumped Adelaide Crows player Andrew Jarman. Port was linked to the controversial player after investigating his availability in the up-coming AFL draft. Page 83.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
